LANDING PR for #717 slice 1: decision 0087's build, the library's base offices are the ones `init` writes, and Brokkr's own picks are brokkr-* offices, so `fast` and `node` install into a fresh folder.

Operator rulings, verbatim:
- 2026-10-17, recorded on #717: option A, one portable base set (quoted in 0087's Context).
- 2026-10-18, on PR #740: "accept all for 740". Recorded on #717 as: decision 0087 accepted as a whole, with every choice its "Asked of the operator" section lists taken as recommended:
  (1) the Brokkr-only layer is agents under other names;
  (2) the `brokkr-` prefix;
  (3) ruling 3: an overlay that writes neither models nor efforts inherits its base's chain and efforts, and efforts without models is refused;
  (4) fast's verifier and shipper stay in slice 1, said so in fast's README, and move in slice 3;
  (5) layout-free charter paths in slice 3;
  (6) the library files are init's serialization, byte for byte under claude with no stack;
  (7) init's chains live in init's table, held by the init_stacks test;
  (8) node's seats lose npx and node, and the folder widens them;
  (9) panel-review stays Brokkr-only.
- Standing ruling 2026-09-30 (re-keyed clones, every scope), extended 2026-10-07 (a refresh whose count shrinks).

Read decision 0087 (docs/decisions/0087-the-base-offices-are-the-ones-init-writes.md) whole first: it is the specification, and its ruling 8 names slice 1's content.

The branch story-717-slice-1 ends at 15bb6e89, cut from main 98f97735. It has two commits:
- 1168d6c9 (story run implement-story-717-recipes-brok-bfc879ed). The run stopped IMPL-BLOCKED on one mechanical blocker only: re-keyed clones the seat's sandbox could not re-baseline. Its review NEVER RAN, so this landing's review is the first.
  - Item 0: 0087 accepted (PR #740), Built partial (#717), Amends: 0078 paired with 0078's Amended by: 0087, the README row, and ruling 3's sentence corrected for dsh.
  - (a) agents/implementer|reviewer|intake.json are init's claude/no-stack serialization byte for byte. init.rs's table is kept and documented as a held copy.
  - (b) the fast-* and node-* overlays write only extends, charter and inputs.
  - (c) overlay.rs: no models and no efforts inherits the base's chain and efforts; efforts without models is refused with exact text. merge_chain CC 7, extended CC 5. Two controls are recorded.
  - (d) the five brokkr-* overlays; recipes/brokkr-fast with a README and prompt budgets (quality/prompt-bytes.json); the re-points (landing and the three wager harnesses to brokkr-fast; panel-review, self, release and triage); the five reason drops.
  - (e) init_stacks::init_writes_the_librarys_portable_base_under_every_agent_cli covers claude, codex and dsh × none, rust and node-npm. It launches through init_stacks' unchanged brokkr_with via a new pub(crate) brokkr_for wrapper that sets HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME under a tempdir, and PATH to one CLI stub for init. Two controls.
  - (f) witnesses.json re-pinned from witness_digests' printed table.
    - Moved: fast, node, landing, wager-harness (and -dsh, -muse), panel-review, self, triage, release, gpt-flash, night-shift, review-first and standby; brokkr-fast added (bundle and table).
    - Stayed: verify, preflight, research, research-dsh, all tables and all charters.
    - This equals ruling 7's forecast. The ruling-7 comparison compiled all 18 recipes at 98f97735 and at head. Manifest agents (with the agent name set aside), hands, capabilities, drivers, boundary, seats and phases are equal for every Brokkr-only recipe, except agent and office NAMES; only fast's and node's hires moved.
  - (g) the new tests/portable_recipes.rs. Per CLI, in a fresh git init + init folder, recipes add fast and node exit 0 with exact report lines, the copies are byte-equal to agents/, and the installed recipe compiles with the folder's base chains and providers (dsh review on claude). Two controls.
  - (h) recipes/fast/README.md says verify fails outside Brokkr until slice 3.
  - Files outside the named scope, each forced by the change:
    - runtime agents/tests.rs, bundle/model_policy_tests.rs and bundle/tier/tests.rs;
    - engine/boundary_tests.rs (three reviewer -> brokkr-reviewer, in decision 0065 slice two's area);
    - tests/{capability_launch,landing_shape,library_data,node_recipe_gates,roster,table_lints,wager_parity}.rs and cli tests/driver_conformance.rs;
    - tests/shelf.rs (ONE expected-refusal line, the removed 'writes no models' text; #737's file);
    - CONTRIBUTING.md's recipe table (+ a brokkr-fast row), docs/status.md, and the census blocks in docs/guides/agent-library.md and recipe-authoring.md;
    - the node, landing and wager-harness (-dsh, -muse) READMEs.
- 15bb6e89 (controller): refreshes quality/jscpd-baseline-tests.json and -data.json for the seven clones the mandated one-line edits re-keyed.
  - The clones: tests 2 (driver_conformance.rs:2218-2219 against engine/boundary_tests.rs:3736-3737); data 5 (brokkr-reviewer.json against review-adversarial.json, recipe-authoring.md:415 against triage's bundle, gpt-flash against triage, the dsh/muse wager bundles, and wager-harness's README against its bundle).
  - jscpd's own --update-baseline: tests 1061 -> 1059 fingerprints, data 233 -> 231. Both shrink. 98f97735's bytes on the flagged files hold, and `quality/ratchet.sh clones` holds.
  - `quality/ratchet.sh baselines 98f97735` names those 7 fingerprints, plus prompt-bytes.json rows for recipes/brokkr-fast/implement (14484) and /review (13515), which were absent before. That is a new recipe 0087 accepted.
- Host gates the implementer ran clean (fmt, clippy, brokkr-runtime --lib 1041, --test it 133, capability_launch 76, brokkr-cli --lib 884, --test it 726, typos, ratchet files and api). Exact coverage runs on the host in this landing.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks below. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns.

Judge, on the HEAD binary and tests:
1. 0087 as built: rulings 1 to 4 and 6, and ruling 8's slice 1, item by item.
   - The three base offices equal init's claude/no-stack serialization byte for byte, and the init_stacks test holds init's table to them across claude, codex and dsh by ruling 1's projection.
   - Each brokkr-* overlay merges to TODAY's definition. Verify by merging and comparing with 98f97735's reviewer/implementer/intake/fast-* files.
   - Each re-point and reason drop is exactly what ruling 4 lists, no more.
   - The portable overlays write only what is theirs.
2. Ruling 3 in overlay.rs: the inheritance and the efforts-without-models refusal are exactly as the decision states, with the refusal's text exact and tested; every other #360 rule (a reason for a power, a reason for nothing refused, one level) is unchanged. Try an overlay writing efforts only, an overlay of an overlay, and a reason for a key neither writes.
3. Ruling 7: reproduce the comparison for at least four Brokkr-only recipes (self, triage, landing, verify). Hires, argv-relevant agent records, hands, capabilities, drivers and boundary must be equal at 98f97735 and HEAD, with only names moved. Confirm every moved and stayed witness against ruling 7's forecast. A moved value outside the forecast is a finding.
4. #717's acceptance for slice 1: recipes add of fast and node in a fresh init folder under each of claude, codex and dsh exits 0, copies the named offices and charters, and the installed recipe compiles. Run one of them yourself through the HEAD binary in a scratch folder with a stub CLI. "Reaches its first seat" (six real runs) is the controller's, after this landing.
5. The out-of-scope files: each edit is forced by the change (a test pinning the old library, a census block, a README now false) and changes nothing else. Name any edit that is not forced.
6. The clone refresh (15bb6e89): the seven fingerprints are re-keys of baselined clones (restore 98f97735's bytes for the flagged files and see clones hold), and the counts shrink.
7. Scope and parallel work: no change to bundle/mcp.rs, adapters/*.json, engine*.rs other than the forced engine/boundary_tests.rs rename, cli_args.rs, doctor*, contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json or reference/. init_stacks.rs's brokkr_with helper is unchanged.
8. For the PR: list the rulings it cites (0087's acceptance for the brokkr-fast prompt-bytes rows and every moved witness; the standing re-keyed-clone ruling for the seven fingerprints), and anything that needs a NEW ruling (none is expected). Name the follow-ups: recipe-authoring.md's composition table (slice 2); 0087's Consequences sentence "Only the operator accepts this proposal"; parked runs on moved digests resuming as drift; the pipeline libraries outside the repo.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051, so the contribution gate can vouch for it.

For the implement phase only: if a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 590); cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test capability_launch --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked (timeout 590; split by FILE:: filters if longer); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and api (clones is the controller's); `cargo crap --path <crate>/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check. A new test file is named *_tests.rs or registered as `mod FILE;` in tests/it.rs.

Other work runs in parallel. Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) has U8a2a in PR #745 (engine.rs, init_stacks.rs's brokkr_with ~248-253), then runs U8a2c (brokkr-protocol hands.rs and children, native_controls/mcp.rs, adapters/mcp.rs, cli hands.rs, lib.rs, probe/observe.rs, doctor.rs, engine/boxed.rs, engine/isolation.rs, engine.rs) and U8a2b (engine/broker.rs, engine.rs). #726 (PR #737) edits brokkr-cli recipes/ and tests/shelf.rs. #288 slice K edits bundle.rs and dialect.rs. #744 edits brokkr-cli tui/ and brokkr-view fleet.rs.

Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. Run every command in the foreground: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

